Resolve citation keys to source file paths via Zotero SQLite

Source: R/zotero.R
crd_zot_src_lookup.Rd

Queries the local Zotero SQLite database to find a PDF or Word document attachment for each of a vector of Better BibTeX citation keys. Returns a tibble suitable for passing to crd_aud_verify_all().

Usage

crd_zot_src_lookup(
  citation_keys,
  zotero_dir = "~/Zotero",
  library = getOption("cred.zotero_library")
)

Arguments

citation_keys

character vector of BBT citation keys to resolve. NA values are silently dropped.

zotero_dir

character(1) path to the Zotero data directory. Default "~/Zotero".

library

The Zotero library to resolve keys in: "user" for My Library, or a group's name or groupID (as in its URL, zotero.org/groups/<groupID>). Zotero's internal libraryID is not accepted: it differs between machines. Default getOption("cred.zotero_library"); NULL searches every library.

Value

A tibble with columns:

  • citation_key (character) — the input key.

  • src_path (character) — absolute path to the attachment file.

  • src_type (character) — "docx" or "pdf".

Only rows where an attachment was found and the file exists on disk are returned. A warning is issued for keys with no resolvable attachment.

Details

A citation key is unique within a Zotero library, not across libraries, so the same key can name different works in My Library and a group library. Name the library with library, or once per session with options(cred.zotero_library = ). With neither, every library is searched, and a key found in more than one is left unresolved with a warning rather than taken from whichever happens to come first. A key shared by two live items within one library is treated the same way.

Trashed items and trashed attachments are never used.

When an item has several attachments, the one taken is the one Zotero itself opens: a PDF before a Word document, then by URL (the attachment whose URL is the item's own, then one with any URL, then one with none), then the oldest. If that file is not on disk the next one is taken. A message names the file taken and the ones left out.

The database is opened read-only and immutable, so a running Zotero is never locked.

Examples

# The toy library shipped with cred holds its items in My Library
toy <- system.file("extdata", package = "cred")
crd_zot_src_lookup(
  c("smith2020SalmonHabitat", "jones2019BeaverEcology"),
  zotero_dir = toy, library = "user"
)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   citation_key           src_path                                       src_type
#>   <chr>                  <chr>                                          <chr>   
#> 1 jones2019BeaverEcology /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/cred/extdata/… docx    
#> 2 smith2020SalmonHabitat /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/cred/extdata/… pdf
